sections.what: San Jose Clinic provides medical, dental, pharmacy, vision and behavioral care to low-income uninsured patients. It operates in Houston and Fort Bend, with eligibility screening and patient financial contributions. Its multidisciplinary services seek to improve access to treatment for people who cannot obtain conventional insured care.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 report shows 4,893 patients and 38,108 appointments. Four confirmed MSA counties account for 4,691 patients; Wharton is excluded. These figures do not demonstrate causal health improvement. Request unique annual households, treatment completion, health outcomes, current audited expenses and alternative-care use.
sections.qualitative: The current annual report identifies 4,893 patients rather than only appointment volume. Original audited statements identify recognized donated medicines and professional resources. The Houston and Fort Bend delivery locations and uninsured eligibility are clear. No current audited expense was recovered; the center transfers a 2022 full-cost denominator to the 2025 patient cohort. Clinical response, household duplication and resource savings are unmeasured hypotheses. Existing charity providers, donated-resource capacity and next-gift additionality remain unresolved. No external trial is used to assert local effect size. Public funding and alternative providers may replace donation-funded care; this requires direct verification.
sections.cost: The conditional reference is $64.94 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 4.470204 clinical QALYs plus -2.056082 income equivalents. Full annual recognized cost is $15,677,822; $10,000 corresponds to 0.001540 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not a demonstrated gift response. The exposed union is 1565.760 household proxies and the clinical subgroup is 313.152 adults. Clinical benefit is union × completion × utility × discounted finite years × geography. Financial successes and other exposed households are disjoint; each has one joint net log. Positive components receive the overlap adjustment before adding full negative components and subtracting full burdens. The resource success share is independent of clinical efficacy, so clinical null retains all resources and costs. Baseline consumption is positive even if reported income is zero. Gains are hypothetical otherwise-paid care or disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, new work expenses and substitution—not retail care values, gross salary or ordinary survivor earnings. One-off participation costs are incremental versus alternative care. Payer stress models distinct counterparty households; central external zero is an unknown-neutral partial-boundary reference, not observed zero or complete world benefit. Unrecognized partner/volunteer costs, broader portfolio benefits and harms, family spillovers and marginal funding response remain unknown.
sections.funding: Original FY2022 expense $15,481,097 plus $196,725 netted donor benefits gives $15,677,822. FY2021 $10,727,257 plus $43,900 gives $10,771,157. FY2020 recognized expense is $10,936,299, but direct-benefit reconciliation remains unverified, so it is not certified comparable. Donated pharmaceuticals, professional services and facility amortization already in the audits are not added again. The current annual report’s $17,185,078 panel is revenue, not expense. Audit opinion dates are not asserted publication dates. Current full costs and marginal capacity are due-diligence blockers.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Reported Harris, Fort Bend, Brazoria and Montgomery count / total; remaining county attribution excluded.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity/public care, recovery supports, insurance eligibility, household behavior and funding replacement; additional response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Patients, appointments, treatment access and finite symptom improvement; appointments are not QALYs.
